industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): diversified industrial groups are cyclical capital goods into a growth scare, but their diversification is itself the simple, proven profile the regime pays for, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: A now, C prior, says the market is paying for it. Three memos this week in this Sector all turn on the Fragility axis, not on the Sector: Beijer Alma (Mixed) and Idun Industrier (Fights it) are small, geared, re-rating-dependent Swedish acquirers, thyssenkrupp (Mixed) is large but 'neither simple nor proven'; the Fragility row carries that judgement, so the Sector row does not double it. One live holding, Sdiptech (5.05%, Sell-side and Thematic Fit A). Counter-case for higher: leadership and six MI Pool names with Thematic Fit B; for lower: the group's small acquirers are what a credit crack hurts first. Neutral by judgement.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack this week, so the condition for B (a confidence print at or above normal with the Riksbank on hold) could not be tested; the only Swedish data point is food retail volumes up 5.3% in September after a value-added tax cut (Danske, 18 Oct), which is a sector fact, not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 0.50%, Hexatronic 4.95%, Sdiptech 5.05%, Xvivo 5.05%, 15.55 points), judged in component 4 and in amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park at SEK 1,808. Progress below about SEK 1,700, where the eighteen-month modal path pays 22% a year and the three-year path 19%; or earlier if the cleared branch's evidence arrives, defined as the FactSet consensus EPS for FY2028 revised up 10% or more with financial net debt to EBITDA at or below 2.5x and the platform-deal pace at four or more a year. Conviction medium, because the arithmetic is clear and the odds on the two branches are the uncertainty. The park has an end: the March 2028 test of the FY2028 consensus, or earlier and toward invalidation if two consecutive quarters pass without a platform deal or a deal is announced above 9x EBITA. The framework's park gates do not park the case (management B, business quality B, predictability C, trackability C); the price and the odds do. The record's one-line bet: a Lifco-lineage acquirer keeps buying at about 7x EBITA inside a 3.0x leverage ceiling while organic growth holds at 3 to 4%, so earnings compound at about 14% a year and the market pays its own median multiple for them; at SEK 1,808 that pays about 17% a year, and 20% only below about SEK 1,700.
case: - Röko is a young Swedish serial acquirer of Lifco lineage whose stall in 2025 was cyclical and whose acquisition engine is running again. At SEK 1,808 the shares pay about 17% a year for that, below the framework's 20% bar, because the price has already recovered 30% from its spring low and the balance sheet that funded the recovery now rations the next leg.

- The change is internal and is the model running harder rather than a new direction. 2025 brought three platform deals, EBITA growth of 9% against a 15% ambition and a management "not satisfied"; 2026 to August brought five platform deals (Lambda SpA, Access Building Products Group, NH Norsk Handel, Fri-Jado consolidated in H1, SEKm 1,249 of annualised sales; CyTech in August as the third Italian platform), a succession that moved the co-founder to full-time sourcing, and leverage taken from 2.0x to 2.6x by choice. On the framework's screen at least three internal forces are strong (acquisitions, balance-sheet utilisation, price rises, new geographies) and the false-positive checks pass; the chief-executive and strategy forces are continuity.

- The external forces are a mild headwind easing, not a tailwind; no force meets the 'Demand Inflection' test. Organic growth went from 0% in Q4 2025 to 6% and 3% in H1 2026 while peers recovered at 5 to 6%, so Röko lags a sector recovery by 150 to 300 basis points; the currency drag on reported results halved from 6% in Q1 to 3% in H1 2026; US tariffs are washing out; the market for acquisitions has tightened (six of eight deals through auctions; Nordic private multiples 8 to 10x EBITDA); sector de-rating contagion after the Lifco short report is the main reason the sector's multiples are at the bottom of their ranges and it can recur.
counter_case: - At the whole-case level, the false friend: Röko is a levered roll-up whose adjusted EBITA grows while its reported earnings, its cash after minorities and its balance sheet decay, so that 21x is not cheap but full for what it is. The evidence: a 27.4% gap between adjusted EBITA (SEKm 1,339) and operating profit (SEKm 1,051) for 2025, with SEKm 242 of acquisition amortisation excluded; an amortisation-to-sales ratio of 4% against 2.5% at Addtech, Indutrade, Lagercrantz and Lifco; option liabilities of SEKm 2,776 that rise SEKm 191 per SEKm 100 of subsidiary EBITA and are charged to equity (SEKm 150 in 2025, SEKm 239 in 2024); 75% average ownership and SEKm 148 of dividends to minorities in 2025; leverage from 2.0x to 2.6x in six months; six of eight deals in auctions with Nordic multiples at 8 to 10x; long-term cash conversion of 60%; no currency hedging with about 90% of sales in foreign currency; 80% cyclical revenue; a lone broker at Hold with a bear case of SEK 1,400. The earnings line the multiple is struck on is 19% above reported (SEK 61.50 against SEK 51.63); the trailing multiple on reported earnings is 35x; the enterprise value the market quotes depends on whether the options are counted as debt, and counting them turns a "fair" 20x EV/EBITA into an "expensive" 22x with nothing changed in the business.

- The record concedes: the option liabilities are debt-like and grow with success; leverage now rations the engine; cash after minorities is about 60% of EBITA, not the 72% headline; entry multiples are rising; the multiple's own history is seventeen months long and its upper half was set in a compounder bull market, so the 8th percentile is weak evidence of cheapness. Its response: the false friend's defining failure, adjusted EBITA up while reported profit contracts, is not observed (reported EPS +7.5% in H1 2026, reported net income +16% in Q2 2026); the amortisation is non-cash and its cash cost is carried through the debt in the return arithmetic; interest-bearing leverage is 0.6x and the options are exercisable over five to ten years and near cash-neutral for net debt on exercise; FactSet free cash flow was 135% of reported net income in FY2025. What the hypothesis wins: its slower version, that the model works but the price already pays for it, is exactly what the modal return of about 17% says; the record holds C not D because the engine runs and the earnings are real, and not B because the hypothesis is right about the price. No claim is made that any asset covers the enterprise value; the 18x trough is a multiple argument, not a cover.
triggers: - The condition that decides the case: the FactSet consensus EPS for FY2028 (mean SEK 88.09, median SEK 92.49 at 2026-09-11; six-month revision already +12.4%) revised up 10% or more by March 2028. Met with the multiple still at 21x: up, and a buy. Unmet at March 2028: the uncleared branch is the case; invalidate.
- Progress triggers: price below about SEK 1,700; or the FY2028 consensus up 10% or more with leverage at or below 2.5x and the deal pace at four or more a year.

- Alarm levels: two consecutive quarters without a platform deal; a deal announced above 9x EBITA (the change-forces report's threshold); financial net debt to EBITDA above 2.7x in any quarter (the earnings review's alarm); organic growth in local currency below 2% for two quarters (moves the odds a full step down; above 5% for two quarters moves them up); net financials above SEKm 200 in FY2027 (consensus about SEKm 150 for FY2026); a second short-seller report on any Swedish compounder; PMI below neutral (the risks report's early warning); reported profit contracting while adjusted EBITA grows (the false friend's failure mode).
- Invalidate levels stated: leverage above the 3.0x ceiling; the FY2028 condition unmet at March 2028.

- Dated steps: Q3 2026 report on 23 October 2026 (first quarter with CyTech and a full Fri-Jado; H2 organic comparison against a weak H2 2025); the FY2026 report and the first dividend decision under the 0 to 20% policy; DNB Carnegie's own test of net debt to EBITDA below 2.3x by year-end 2026; the first year-on-year comparison of Fri-Jado; the midpoint of the five-year doubling ambition in months eighteen to thirty-six.

- Series to watch: acquisition announcements (count, size, stated multiple); quarterly organic growth in local currency, financial net debt to EBITDA, cash conversion, segment margins; peers' quarterly organic growth (Lifco, Indutrade, Lagercrantz); EUR/SEK and GBP/SEK and STIBOR daily; European consumer confidence and Eurozone and Swedish PMIs monthly; average ownership of subsidiaries (about 75% towards about 85%); minority share of profit (about 25%); net working capital (26.0% of revenue); relative strength percentile (37); average daily value traded (USD 2.2m). The company's own series are quarterly; the missing series is subsidiary-level.
